status: Admitted native stack growth is accounted separately for each target, workload and temperature.
scope: Temporary heap bytes, retained heap bytes and whole-call stack, separately by target, feature configuration and completed workload. Existing binary-size accounts remain independent.
cumulative_rule: Before the first admission for a workload, measure the fixed baseline, current baseline and candidate. Preserve any prior positive growth and every subsequent positive charge. Do not net decreases against increases or transfer headroom between targets, metrics or workloads. Missing historical or equivalent completed controls require explicit evidence and a documented baseline decision, not an assumed zero charge.

accounts.target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, Rust 1.95.0 release, System allocator, one guarded native worker
accounts.call_boundary: Construct problem and radii, warm approximate predicate for opaque inputs, certify, inspect status and destroy complete report. Thread startup and caller frames excluded from stack; guard and caller included in headroom.
accounts.workload_key: i = (0 report or 1 Krawczyk)*30 + (0 affine, 1 univariate quadratic, 2 multivariate quadratic)*10 + (0 STRICT or 1 APPROXIMATE_512)*5 + radius case (0 hidden negative, 1 one, 2 zero, 3 negative one, 4 opaque positive)
accounts.measurement: Two sentinel patterns, cold and warm, 24 processes per revision. Positive differences between observed maxima charged separately even where individual samples vary. Full 120 rows in memory-rows.json in the archive. Zero-charge rows have full remaining allowance.

accounts.target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, glibc, Rust 1.95.0 release, one worker
accounts.benefit: Complete exact queries for finite and split dyadic sets without materializing a common grid or filling real gaps.
accounts.scope: Prepared queries and complete construction, comparison, retry and drop. Complete extended division is a separate unchanged control. Cold and warm calls have separate accounts.
accounts.measurement: Twelve fresh processes per revision per lock. Two 1-byte-resolution stack sentinel patterns in each cold/warm case. Fixed/previous/retained results for all 580 metrics are in isolated-memory-confirmed.json. Requested/usable heap, RSS and returned geometry or error are recorded separately.

accounts.target: Rust 1.95.0 x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release, one guarded Linux worker
accounts.call_boundary: Construct problem and bounds, execute certificate, inspect result and drop output. Two watermark patterns, cold and warm workers. Allocation counts and traffic are recorded separately from observed live bytes.

regular_workloads.previous_charge_rule: Carry prior positive charges. Charge any positive difference from either the archived previous maximum or the remeasurement of the same binary.

stress_workloads.workload_key: i = 6*policy + case; policies STRICT/APPROXIMATE_512. Cases 0..5 are affine/univariate/multivariate point containment, coupled affine elimination, univariate/multivariate contraction.
stress_workloads.comparison: For corrected cases 8 and 11 use the same input and previously completed STRICT proof. Record the raw prior same-policy result separately. Other keys compare identical policies, including unchanged unsupported proof behavior in the other certifiers.

limitations: No allocation-free firmware or configured RAM/task-stack limit is relaxed.
Runtime, predicate/dispatch order, exact outputs and certainty remain separate gates.
No candidate is admitted solely by this policy record.

wasip1_qualification.target: Rust 1.95 wasm32-wasip1, opt-in scalar and mixed lattice/dyadic release conformance clients
wasip1_qualification.basis: New target registration. All previously selected default artifacts remain byte-identical. Existing successful fixed-only WASI work is measured before and after selection. New mixed arithmetic is compared with the previously supported bare workload and the automatic same-ABI prototype. The stack and requested-heap observations match the controls. Bare dyadic conversion committed one extra 64 KiB linear-memory page; ordinary Preview 1 stayed at its initial capacity. No positive memory exception is charged.
wasip1_qualification.memory_model: Single guest instance at a time. Cold/warm, two fresh instances with complementary stack fills. Record original linked primitive writes, instrumented SP minima, and Rust system allocator requests in the standard-library clients, including releases through completed output. Guest linear memory never grew. Engine/host memory is outside this account.

whole_solver_wasi_qualification.workload: Compiled 70-executable Hypersolve qualification job on Linux. Warm Cargo lookup, native and WASI libtest, Python, Node, children, assertion output and cleanup in one fresh cgroup v2 per compiler and workload. Swap disabled.
whole_solver_wasi_qualification.positive_charges: New qualification workload. Record its full observed peak against its own capacity. The preceding run executed 64 direct tests and the two migration comparisons. Its separate reference peak measures the change in the CI job. No production allocation or stack allowance is spent. Cold compilation is outside this observation.

produced_tensor_coefficient_qualificatio.workload: Compiled whole Hypersolve native/WASI qualification job with the additional width and rational-denominator cases. Warm Cargo lookup, children and cleanup inside a fresh swap-disabled Linux cgroup. Compilation is outside this account.
produced_tensor_coefficient_qualificatio.charge: Keep the previously registered full peak plus positive growth. This is a test workload account. All production stack and heap accounts carry forward.

whole_scalar_wasi_qualification.scope: New hosted Hyperinterval test job, one compiler lane and one child guest at a time. One fresh swap-disabled cgroup per run. Linux memory.peak includes parent, children, Cargo, native test relinking, Node and cleanup, with dependency and guest build caches prewarmed. Cold dependency compilation is separate. Native-only and guest-only five-case runs are separate compiled workloads.
whole_scalar_wasi_qualification.charge: Register the entire observed peak per compiler for the new job, without offsetting production, firmware or other test budgets. Existing ordinary production heap and stack accounts carry forward.

fixed_hull_fuzz_campaign.scope: Hosted sanitizer conformance campaigns only. Fresh swap-disabled cgroup per invocation through result and cleanup. One worker, ASan quarantine 128 MiB, max 100000 runs, 30 s, 16 or 32 input bytes. The baseline and candidate legacy invocations consume the same input seeds. The new workload includes both formats. Production heap and stack accounts carry forward independently.
fixed_hull_fuzz_campaign.unit: whole cgroup peak bytes, including input corpus reads, fuzzer, sanitizer and allocator overhead

periodic_refinement_qualification.scope: One freshly instantiated compiled test job, sequential cases, inside a swap-disabled Linux cgroup, including native or Node/WASI startup through process exit. Separately charge the complete warmed scalar conformance job against its existing register. Production heap and stack accounts carry forward.

rational_periodic_ingress.scope: Four rational periodic calls, ordinary and generated sources, native and guest execution, denial, completed outputs and retries. complete-memory-details.json lists both dependency locks and every per-workload account. Includes separate whole-ownership epochs from fresh processes through input/output destruction. Compiler and OS job peaks are separate.

scalar_query_test.scope: Native Hyperreal integration executable and the identical maintained Rust fixture in a portable WASI consumer. Both with and without trace. Same new-test file/job caps.

monotone_composition_qualification.scope: One compiled release test process with sequential cases, including native startup or Node/WASI instantiation through exit. Full warmed conformance jobs use the existing cumulative account. Production sources are identical to the preceding revision.

wasm_float_endpoint_qualification_jobs.scope: New host-process account for one sequential Node primitive verifier from startup through result publication and exit, including 24 isolated endpoint traps. Independent from the existing guest stack and allocator accounts. Paired measurements use the identical module, corpus and Node runtime; cgroup peaks include the measuring Python process.

shared_timing_evidence_reference_job.scope: Native host test process and observer from spawn through result and exit, two-participant exact retiming, global job publication and drop. Test assertion borrows the existing record and a static expected slice. Production code is unchanged.
shared_timing_evidence_reference_job.measurement: Fresh cgroup v2 memory.peak for each run, including the Python observer. This is a complete group capacity check, not an allocation or stack measurement. The three repetitions at each revision use the same completed test.

dq_simulator_full_counter.scope: Native simulator unit-test suite and external client making one million accepted and one million rejected public calls. Three fresh full-process group lifetimes per compiler, revision and artifact. Peak includes the Python observer. The counter repair uses existing fields and allocates no heap storage. No on-board stack or memory qualification is claimed.
dq_simulator_full_counter.requested_heap: glibc libmemusage interposition on the linked executables with a common argv[0]. Three fresh instrumented jobs for each stage. Requested peaks and all recorded malloc, calloc, realloc and free counts and bytes agree. Group peaks include the observer and runtime variability.
dq_simulator_full_counter.stack_scope: Maximum observed rsp-based DWARF CFA offset per emitted client frame. A null value is censored. Inlining differs by compiler. These observations do not bound OS startup or whole-thread stack.

ieee_power_qualification.scope: Completed sequential Node arithmetic verification with 24 fresh trap checks, and Python generation through publication of the deterministic corpus. Host group peaks include the observer. Previous positive verifier charges carry forward. The generator at its first commit 0ba14a211 has the same source blob as the predecessor.
ieee_power_qualification.positive_incremental_cap: minimum of 4 MiB and 5% of the preceding measured peak
ieee_power_qualification.positive_cumulative_cap: minimum of 8 MiB and 10% of the fixed preceding peak

quadratic_alpha_proof_classification.workload: 63 quadratic rows per evaluation, both policies, 1 and 7 repetitions; complete model construction, proof classification, field checks and destruction. One native worker or WASI instance per process.
quadratic_alpha_proof_classification.scope: No positive memory charge on common workloads. Fixed, previous and retained stack, requested heap, allocator counts and bytes freed agree. Opaque unresolved input is a separate correctly completed workload.
